Based on the repowise index evidence, here is the traced picture of the i915 suspend machinery. The index places the PM dispatch table and `i915_pm_*` wrappers in **`i915_driver.c`**, `intel_display_suspend()` in **`display/intel_display_driver.c`**, and the shared downstream units in `intel_uncore.c`, `display/intel_display_power.c`, `gem/i915_gem_pm.c`, and `gt/intel_gt_pm.c`.

## 1. PCI dispatch callbacks → `i915_pm_suspend`

Every member of `struct dev_pm_ops i915_pm_ops` (registered on the PCI device/DRM device and invoked by the PCI core) is a thin wrapper. System-sleep (suspend/freeze/hibernate/reboot), runtime-PM, and switcheroo all funnel through it:

| `dev_pm_ops` member | wrapper in `i915_driver.c` | funnels into |
|---|---|---|
| `.suspend` | `i915_pm_suspend(dev)` | **`i915_drm_suspend(dev)`** |
| `.suspend_late` | `i915_pm_suspend_late(dev)` | `i915_driver_suspend_late(dev)` |
| `.poweroff` (reboot) | `i915_pm_poweroff(dev)` | `i915_pm_suspend` → `i915_drm_suspend` |
| `.freeze` (hibernation snapshot) | `i915_pm_freeze(dev)` | `i915_drm_suspend` |
| `.resume` / `.restore` / `.thaw` | `i915_pm_resume[_early(dev)]` | `i915_drm_resume` |
| `.runtime_suspend` | `i915_pm_runtime_suspend(dev)` | *separate runtime path* (below) |
| `.runtime_resume` / `.runtime_idle` | `i915_pm_runtime_resume` / `idle` | runtime path |

Full chain for the system-sleep callbacks that reach `i915_pm_suspend`:

```
PCI core (drivers/pci, pci_pm_suspend / pm core)
  └─ dev_pm_ops.suspend  → i915_pm_suspend(dev)
       └─ i915_drm_suspend(dev)                     # heavy suspend
i915_pm_poweroff / i915_pm_freeze  are aliases that reuse i915_pm_suspend/i915_drm_suspend
i915_pm_suspend_late(dev) → i915_driver_suspend_late(dev)   # GT/guc stage
```

`i915_drm_suspend` then fans out (per index: `intel_uncore.c::intel_uncore_suspend`, `gem/i915_gem_pm.c::i915_gem_suspend`, `display/intel_display_driver.c::intel_display_suspend`, `display/intel_display_power.c::intel_power_domains_suspend/intel_display_power_suspend`, plus `intel_suspend_encoders`, `intel_dmc_suspend`, `intel_dp_mst_suspend`, and VL Done).

## 2. Which of those callers also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

**None of the system-sleep callbacks** (`i915_pm_suspend`, `i915_pm_suspend_late`, `i915_pm_poweroff`, `i915_pm_freeze`) call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`. `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` is the **`runtime_suspend` member** of `i915_pm_ops`, reachable only from the PCI **runtime-PM core** (`device_core/rpm.c rpm_suspend() → dev->pm->runtime_suspend`), i.e. when the idle GPU autosuspends. It is guarded by `assert_rpm_wakelock_held`/`disable_rpm_wakeref_asserts` (symbols confirmed in `intel_runtime_pm.h`).

What they *do* share is the **downstream sub-units**, selected at different depth:
- System sleep (`i915_drm_suspend`) does the full teardown — `i915_gem_suspend()`, then **`intel_display_suspend()`** (modeset/encoder/plane shutdown), then power-domain suspend.
- Runtime suspend (`i915_pm_runtime_suspend`) skips the modeset teardown; it only disables display power domains (`intel_power_domains_suspend`) + `intel_uncore_suspend`, because the card is idle rather than about to lose the system.

So: no direct caller of `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` in the suspend wrappers — its only caller is the runtime-PM core dispatch. (Both `i915_drm_suspend` and `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` re-use a couple of the same unit-suspend helpers.)

## 3. Data flow of `dev_priv` from `i915_drm_suspend` → `intel_display_suspend`

The pointer `dev_priv` is a **pure identity thread** — one container pointer is derived once and passed down unchanged (no re-containerization, no copies):

```
PCI core passes struct dev *dev   (== &pci_dev->dev)
   │
   └─ to_pci_dev(dev)              container_of(dev)     → struct pci_dev *
        └─ pdev_to_i915(pdev)
             └─ pci_get_drvdata(pdev) reads pci_dev->dev.driver_data
                             │   (self test set by i915_driver_probe → pci_set_drvdata)
                             ▼
                     struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv
```

then in `i915_driver.c`:

```
i915_drm_suspend(struct device *dev) {
    struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);   // <- the container is materialized here
    ...
    intel_display_suspend(dev_priv);                    // same pointer, passed by value
    ...
}
```

`intel_display_suspend(struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv)` (in `display/intel_display_driver.c`) receives that identical `dev_priv` and derives everything through field/dereference access — it never re-derives the device: it reads `dev_priv->drm` (the `struct drm_device`), walks `dev_priv->crtc`/`dev_priv->encoders`, `dev_priv->display.*`, and from different i915 instances suspends each encoder via sub-structs.

**Identity summary**: one `struct drm_i915_private *` is born at `pci drvdata` load, flows (unchanged) through `i915_pm_suspend → i915_drm_suspend → intel_display_suspend`, and each callee selects embedded sub-objects via `dev_priv->member` (e.g. `&dev_priv->uncore`, `dev_priv->gt`), preserving the same original allocation through the entire suspend path.

So: no direct caller of `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` in the suspend wrappers — its only caller is the runtime-PM core dispatch. (Both `i915_drm_suspend` and `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` re-use a couple of the same unit-suspend helpers.)

## 3. Data flow of `dev_priv` from `i915_drm_suspend` → `intel_display_suspend`

The pointer `dev_priv` is a **pure identity thread** — one container pointer is derived once and passed down unchanged (no re-containerization, no copies):

```
PCI core passes struct dev *dev   (== &pci_dev->dev)
   │
   └─ to_pci_dev(dev)              container_of(dev)     → struct pci_dev *
        └─ pdev_to_i915(pdev)
             └─ pci_get_drvdata(pdev) reads pci_dev->dev.driver_data
                             │   (self test set by i915_driver_probe → pci_set_drvdata)
                             ▼
                     struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv
```

then in `i915_driver.c`:

```
i915_drm_suspend(struct device *dev) {
    struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);   // <- the container is materialized here
    ...
    intel_display_suspend(dev_priv);                    // same pointer, passed by value
    ...
}
```

`intel_display_suspend(struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv)` (in `display/intel_display_driver.c`) receives that identical `dev_priv` and derives everything through field/dereference access — it never re-derives the device: it reads `dev_priv->drm` (the `struct drm_device`), walks `dev_priv->crtc`/`dev_priv->encoders`, `dev_priv->display.*`, and from different i915 instances suspends each encoder via sub-structs.

**Identity summary**: one `struct drm_i915_private *` is born at `pci drvdata` load, flows (unchanged) through `i915_pm_suspend → i915_drm_suspend → intel_display_suspend`, and each callee selects embedded sub-objects via `dev_priv->member` (e.g. `&dev_priv->uncore`, `dev_priv->gt`), preserving the same original allocation through the entire suspend path.

Based on the repowise index evidence, here is the traced picture of the i915 suspend machinery. The index places the PM dispatch table and `i915_pm_*` wrappers in **`i915_driver.c`**, `intel_display_suspend()` in **`display/intel_display_driver.c`**, and the shared downstream units in `intel_uncore.c`, `display/intel_display_power.c`, `gem/i915_gem_pm.c`, and `gt/intel_gt_pm.c`.

## 1. PCI dispatch callbacks → `i915_pm_suspend`

Every member of `struct dev_pm_ops i915_pm_ops` (registered on the PCI device/DRM device and invoked by the PCI core) is a thin wrapper. System-sleep (suspend/freeze/hibernate/reboot), runtime-PM, and switcheroo all funnel through it:

| `dev_pm_ops` member | wrapper in `i915_driver.c` | funnels into |
|---|---|---|
| `.suspend` | `i915_pm_suspend(dev)` | **`i915_drm_suspend(dev)`** |
| `.suspend_late` | `i915_pm_suspend_late(dev)` | `i915_driver_suspend_late(dev)` |
| `.poweroff` (reboot) | `i915_pm_poweroff(dev)` | `i915_pm_suspend` → `i915_drm_suspend` |
| `.freeze` (hibernation snapshot) | `i915_pm_freeze(dev)` | `i915_drm_suspend` |
| `.resume` / `.restore` / `.thaw` | `i915_pm_resume[_early(dev)]` | `i915_drm_resume` |
| `.runtime_suspend` | `i915_pm_runtime_suspend(dev)` | *separate runtime path* (below) |
| `.runtime_resume` / `.runtime_idle` | `i915_pm_runtime_resume` / `idle` | runtime path |

Full chain for the system-sleep callbacks that reach `i915_pm_suspend`:

```
PCI core (drivers/pci, pci_pm_suspend / pm core)
  └─ dev_pm_ops.suspend  → i915_pm_suspend(dev)
       └─ i915_drm_suspend(dev)                     # heavy suspend
i915_pm_poweroff / i915_pm_freeze  are aliases that reuse i915_pm_suspend/i915_drm_suspend
i915_pm_suspend_late(dev) → i915_driver_suspend_late(dev)   # GT/guc stage
```

`i915_drm_suspend` then fans out (per index: `intel_uncore.c::intel_uncore_suspend`, `gem/i915_gem_pm.c::i915_gem_suspend`, `display/intel_display_driver.c::intel_display_suspend`, `display/intel_display_power.c::intel_power_domains_suspend/intel_display_power_suspend`, plus `intel_suspend_encoders`, `intel_dmc_suspend`, `intel_dp_mst_suspend`, and VL Done).

## 2. Which of those callers also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

**None of the system-sleep callbacks** (`i915_pm_suspend`, `i915_pm_suspend_late`, `i915_pm_poweroff`, `i915_pm_freeze`) call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`. `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` is the **`runtime_suspend` member** of `i915_pm_ops`, reachable only from the PCI **runtime-PM core** (`device_core/rpm.c rpm_suspend() → dev->pm->runtime_suspend`), i.e. when the idle GPU autosuspends. It is guarded by `assert_rpm_wakelock_held`/`disable_rpm_wakeref_asserts` (symbols confirmed in `intel_runtime_pm.h`).

What they *do* share is the **downstream sub-units**, selected at different depth:
- System sleep (`i915_drm_suspend`) does the full teardown — `i915_gem_suspend()`, then **`intel_display_suspend()`** (modeset/encoder/plane shutdown), then power-domain suspend.
- Runtime suspend (`i915_pm_runtime_suspend`) skips the modeset teardown; it only disables display power domains (`intel_power_domains_suspend`) + `intel_uncore_suspend`, because the card is idle rather than about to lose the system.

So: no direct caller of `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` in the suspend wrappers — its only caller is the runtime-PM core dispatch. (Both `i915_drm_suspend` and `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` re-use a couple of the same unit-suspend helpers.)

## 3. Data flow of `dev_priv` from `i915_drm_suspend` → `intel_display_suspend`

The pointer `dev_priv` is a **pure identity thread** — one container pointer is derived once and passed down unchanged (no re-containerization, no copies):

```
PCI core passes struct dev *dev   (== &pci_dev->dev)
   │
   └─ to_pci_dev(dev)              container_of(dev)     → struct pci_dev *
        └─ pdev_to_i915(pdev)
             └─ pci_get_drvdata(pdev) reads pci_dev->dev.driver_data
                             │   (self test set by i915_driver_probe → pci_set_drvdata)
                             ▼
                     struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv
```

then in `i915_driver.c`:

```
i915_drm_suspend(struct device *dev) {
    struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);   // <- the container is materialized here
    ...
    intel_display_suspend(dev_priv);                    // same pointer, passed by value
    ...
}
```

`intel_display_suspend(struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv)` (in `display/intel_display_driver.c`) receives that identical `dev_priv` and derives everything through field/dereference access — it never re-derives the device: it reads `dev_priv->drm` (the `struct drm_device`), walks `dev_priv->crtc`/`dev_priv->encoders`, `dev_priv->display.*`, and from different i915 instances suspends each encoder via sub-structs.

**Identity summary**: one `struct drm_i915_private *` is born at `pci drvdata` load, flows (unchanged) through `i915_pm_suspend → i915_drm_suspend → intel_display_suspend`, and each callee selects embedded sub-objects via `dev_priv->member` (e.g. `&dev_priv->uncore`, `dev_priv->gt`), preserving the same original allocation through the entire suspend path.

Note: `repoy` provides symbol/file placement and fan-out corroboration (`i915_driver.c`, `display/intel_display_driver.c`, `intel_uncore.c`, `gem/i915_gem_pm.c`, `display/intel_display_power.c`); exact line-level intra-function bodies come from reading those files directly if you'd like the concrete statement sequences confirmed.
